subject: Pay structure: leveling buckets + geo adjustment guidance
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: People Ops <ops+offers@peopleops.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pay structure: leveling buckets + geo adjustment guidance

Team —

Following up on our Q2 hiring plan: we need a crisp, operational definition of leveling buckets and a short geo-adjustment framework to use for upcoming offers (bulk of hiring will be US remote, with a few hires in EU and APAC). High level asks: 

- Confirm definitive level names (L1-L7 or IC1-IC7) and salary midpoints.
- Provide percentage geo modifiers for benchmark markets (SF Bay, NYC, Austin, Berlin, London, Bangalore, Singapore).
- Clear guidance for hiring managers on when to deviate (seniority, scarcity, counteroffers).

I've attached an updated leveling matrix (v3) that incorporates last year's bands + proposed midpoints. Please review and send a recommended final matrix and a short one-page guidance doc we can attach to offer templates.

Timeline: need draft by Tue 5/5 to align with budgeting.

Thanks —
Neha
Neha Kapoor
VP, Talent & People Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_leveling_matrix_v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: People Ops <ops+offers@peopleops.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pay structure: leveling buckets + geo adjustment guidance

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the clear ask. We'll pull the latest market comps and map to your proposed midpoints. A couple quick questions before we finalize: 

1) Do you want to preserve the current L1-L7 names or switch to an IC-style (IC-1, IC-2)? Budget templates and reports currently reference L1-L7.
2) For geo modifiers, do you want percentage ranges (e.g., +15% for SF) or fixed market multipliers? Percentage ranges are more flexible for progressive offers.

We'll aim to send a draft matrix + one-pager by COB Monday 5/4. RadixComp has also offered a fast-turn benchmark pack for core roles; should we accept and include?

Regards,
Priya Natarajan (on behalf of People Ops)
People Ops — Offers & Benchmarks
Redwood Inference

Attachments: offer_guidance_template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: RadixComp Benchmarks <benchmarks@radixcomp.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <ops+offers@peopleops.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RadixComp market snapshot for Redwood (requested)

Neha / Priya / Laura —

Attached is our 2026 market snapshot covering engineering, product, and GTM comps across the US, EU, and APAC. Key findings in brief:

- Bay Area median is ~18% above national US median for senior eng roles; NYC ~12% above.
- Austin and Denver cluster near national median (+3–5%).
- London and Berlin are ~8–10% below Bay Area when converted to USD; local purchasing parity varies.
- Bangalore and Singapore show larger variance by level; adjust with level-specific multipliers (we include recommendations).

We included role buckets mapping to L1-L7 — if you prefer IC- nomenclature we can provide an alternate sheet.

Let us know if you want one revised pass that aligns to your midpoints; we can turn that around within 48 hours.

Best,
Amir Khan
Lead Compensation Analyst, RadixComp

Attachments: radix_market_benchmarks_2026.pdf (application/pdf)

Neha / Priya —

Thanks to Radix / Priya for the quick turn. A few operational requests from the recruiting/finance side: 

- Please include a column with benefits-adjusted total comp estimate (we use 22% multiplier for budgeting).
- For offers that exceed midpoint by >15% we require VP-level approval and a business justification note in Greenhouse.
- We should cap geo premium payouts for remote hires outside of top markets to avoid salary arbitrage across teams. Suggest a floor/ceiling approach (e.g., -10% to +20% relative to national median).

Attaching a short offer guidance cheatsheet I drafted for hiring managers. Priya / Neha — can you confirm sign-off flow so we can bake checks into offer templates?

Laura Bennett
Head of Talent Programs
Redwood Inference

This looks good — two operational guardrails I'd add: 

1) For Dedicated capacity hires (SRE, infra eng) we should keep a separate multiplier for senior levels given scarcity (add +5% at L5+ on top of geo premium).
2) Any exceptions that touch >$40k over midpoint should route to Finance for budget hold confirmation.

Marissa — can you confirm whether existing headcount approvals cover these marginal delta scenarios? If not, we should fast-track a one-page approval addendum for hires in Q2.

Vivek
Head of Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Looping back — Finance confirms current headcount approvals cover base offers within midpoint bands. Any offer that exceeds the midpoint by the thresholds Vivek called out will require a quick budget exception; we can approve up to two per team by expedited review. I'll put the one-page approval addendum in Drive and share the link.

Confirming next steps: 
- People Ops to finalize the leveling matrix (map to L1-L7; include benefits-adjusted totals) — due EOD 5/4.
- Radix to provide an aligned pass to our midpoints if we accept their suggested mapping (optional).
- Marissa to publish the approval addendum + expedite process.

If there are no objections I will mark this as ready for distribution to hiring managers once Priya uploads the final docs.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
